questions.question: What are the essential sections a brand style guide should include?
questions.answer_summary: A commonly cited framework lists seven: brand story, logo usage rules (including what's NOT allowed), exact color codes (Pantone/RGB/HEX/CMYK), typography rules, photography mood boards, illustration guidelines, and brand voice.

questions.question: Should a style guide explain why design decisions were made, not just list the rules?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — one branding-agency analysis flags 'missing strategic rationale' (guidelines that exist without explaining why decisions were made) as a critical failure of basic style guides.

questions.question: Why do employees or partner teams end up ignoring the official style guide?
questions.answer_summary: A commonly cited reason is that guides become 'overly complex PDFs that teams ignore rather than reference' instead of being a living, easy-to-use source of truth.

questions.question: Is 'less is more' good advice when writing a style guide?
questions.answer_summary: No — one design-agency guide states 'less is more doesn't apply to style guides — you should be as detailed as possible,' specifically calling out logo variations, exact color codes, and voice guidance as areas needing detail.

questions.question: Does a brand system need to work for automated/AI systems now, not just human readers?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — one branding analysis explicitly notes brands 'now need to work for humans, staff, and AI algorithms that verify and recommend,' beyond single-audience visual design.

questions.question: What's an example of a real, published brand style guide?
questions.answer_summary: Mailchimp publishes its brand assets/style guide publicly, and public-sector examples such as WMATA (Washington DC Metro) have published brand and style guideline PDFs that get referenced online.

questions.question: Do most 'free brand style guide generator' tools cover strategy, or just visual assets?
questions.answer_summary: Evidence suggests most easily found generator tools focus on assembling visual assets (logo, colors, fonts) rather than the strategic rationale or governance layer that agency-side write-ups say a real guide needs.
